Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J
1. Mr. Manoj Kumar & Mr. Piyush Tiwari,
learned Central Government Standing Counsel
for the petitioner.
2. Since common questions of law and fact
are involved in these petitions, therefore, they
are being heard and decided together.
However, for the sake of brevity and
convenience, facts of WPMS No. 2873 of 2026
alone are being considered and discussed.
3. Certain persons moved an application for
gratuity under Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972.
The said application was allowed by
Controlling Authority vide order dated
18.12.2024. Petitioner filed appeal under
Section 7(7) of the Payment of Gratuity Act,
1972, which was dismissed on the ground of
delay vide order dated 23.06.2026. Thus,
feeling aggrieved, petitioner has approached
this Court challenging the order passed by
Appellate Authority/Deputy Chief Labour
Commissioner (Central), Dehradun. The order
passed by Controlling Authority, under Section
7(4)(c) of the Act is also challenged.
4. Sub-Section (7) of Section 7 of Payment
of Gratuity Act provides for an appeal against
order passed by Controlling Authority and
provides that limitation for filing such appeal
shall be 60 days from the date of receipt of
the order. First proviso to Sub-Section (7) of

UKHC010167302026
2026:UHC:9108
Section 7 of the Act, however, provides that
limitation period of sixty days is extendable
for further period of sixty days, if sufficient
cause is shown by the appellant for not fling
the appeal within limitation period of sixty
days. Thus, under no circumstances, an
appeal, filed beyond 60 + 60 = 120 days from
the date of receipt of the order, can be
entertained.
5. Sub-Section (7) of Section 7 of the Act is
extracted below for ready reference:-
"(7) Any person aggrieved by an order under sub-section (4), may, within sixty days from the date of the
receipt of the order, prefer an appeal to the appropriate
Government or such other authority as may be specified
by the appropriate Government in this behalf:
Provided that the appropriate Government or the
appellate authority, as the case may be, may, if it is
satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient
cause from preferring the appeal within the said period
of sixty days, extend the said period by a further period
of sixty days.
39 [Provided further that no appeal by an employer shall
be admitted unless at the time of preferring the appeal,
the appellant either produces a certificate of the
controlling authority to the effect that the appellant has
deposited with him an amount equal to the amount of
gratuity required to be deposited under sub-section (4),
or deposits with the appellate authority such amount.]"
6. On a plain reading of the aforesaid
provision, it becomes luminously clear that
the Appellate Authority has jurisdiction to
condone the delay beyond the period of sixty
days, if sufficient cause is shown, by
extending the said period for a further period
of sixty days. Payment of Gratuity Act is
special statute; it prescribed limitation period
for filing appeal and also contains a provision
prescribing the maximum period within which
an appeal has to be filed. Thus, the power of
the appropriate Government or the Appellate
Authority to condone the delay is
circumscribed and delay beyond 120 days,
from the date of receipt of the order, is not
condonable.
7. In the case of Chhattisgarh State
Electricity Board vs. Central Electricity

UKHC010167302026
2026:UHC:9108
Regulatory Commission & others, reported as
(2010) 5 SCC 23, Hon'ble Supreme Court,
while considering Section 125 of the Electricity
Act, 2003 held as under:-
"25. Section 125 lays down that any person aggrieved by
any decision or order of the Tribunal can file an appeal to
this Court within 60 days from the date of communication
of the decision or order of the Tribunal. Proviso to Section
125 empowers this Court to entertain an appeal filed
within a further period of 60 days if it is satisfied that
there was sufficient cause for not filing appeal within the
initial period of 60 days. This shows that the period of
limitation prescribed for filing appeals under Sections
111(2) and 125 is substantially different from the period
prescribed under the Limitation Act for filing suits, etc. The
use of the expression "within a further period of not
exceeding 60 days" in the proviso to Section 125 makes it
clear that the outer limit for filing an appeal is 120 days.
There is no provision in the Act under which this Court can
entertain an appeal filed against the decision or order of
the Tribunal after more than 120 days."
8. Learned counsel for the petitioner
contends that as many as 29 persons
approached the Controlling Authority by
making one composite application under
Section 7(4)(b) of Payment of Gratuity Act;
however, Controlling Authority passed twenty
orders on 12.12.2024 and nine orders on
18.12.2024. He submits that these orders
were received in the Office of the petitioner on
26.12.2024 and the appeal was filed by
petitioner within 120 days i.e. on 12.03.2025.,
after receiving the order passed by Controlling
Authority.
9. He, however, points out that a single
appeal was filed against 29 orders passed by
Controlling Authority and the appeal filed by
petitioner, however, was returned by the
Appellate Authority vide letter dated
10.10.2025 and petitioner was asked to file
separate appeals, with certified copy of the
order passed by Controlling Authority and
valid bank-draft.
10. Learned counsel for the petitioner thus
contends that appeal was filed by petitioner
within Statutory period of 120 days, however,
the said appeal was returned to petitioner on

UKHC010167302026
2026:UHC:9108
10.10.2025, and petitioner thereafter filed 29
separate appeals on 31.10.2025, therefore,
petitioner is not at fault and the appeal filed
by petitioner, in terms of letter dated
10.10.2025 issued by Appellate Authority,
could not have been dismissed on the ground
of delay.
11. This Court is not impressed by the
contention raised on behalf of petitioner.
Section 7(4)(b) of Payment of Gratuity Act
provides that whenever there is a dispute
regarding the amount of gratuity payable to
an employee, such dispute shall be taken to
the Controlling Authority for decision. There is
nothing in Section 7(4)(b) to indicate that two
or more similarly situate persons cannot
jointly file an application before the
Controlling Authority. Section 7(7) of the Act,
however, contemplates separate appeal for
each order. Thus, the composite appeal,
against 29 orders filed by petitioner in the
month of March, was rightly not entertained.
Since petitioner filed appeal, as per mandate
of Section 7(7) of the Act only on 31.10.2025,
therefore, learned Appellate Authority was
justified in dismissing the appeal on the
ground of delay.
12. Learned counsel for the petitioner relies
upon a judgment rendered by Hon'ble Kerala
High Court in the case of Nataraja Pillai vs.
Regional Joint Labour Commissioner & others
(Original Petition No. 10302 of 1992-B, dated
22.10.1992), reported as (1993) 1 LLN 721.
Para 5 of the said judgment, on which heavy
reliance was placed by learned counsel for the
petitioner, is reproduced below:-
"5. It is the case of the petitioner that there was no
application to condone the delay giving sufficient reasons
for the belated presentation of the application. Learned
counsel appearing for the third respondent submitted that
before making the formal application, Exhibit P-1, the third
respondent had submitted an application which is marked
as Exhibit P-3 (a) by the appellate authority. I went
through Exhibit P-3(a) and found that the third respondent
has given some reasons for not being able to present the
application earlier. No doubt, Exhibit P-3 order does not

UKHC010167302026
2026:UHC:9108
disclose that it was specifically considered. Nothing has
been stated in the order about the delay. A reading of the
proviso to Rule 10 indicates that a separate petition to
condone the delay is not mandatory and the only
requirement is that the authority must be satisfied that
there is sufficient cause for the delay in presenting the
application. It is true that in the objection filed by the
petitioner, specific point has been raised in regard to the
delay in filing the representation. The very fact that the
controlling authority accepted the application on file and
chose to consider it on merits indicates that he was
satisfied with the reasons stated by the petitioner in Exhibit
P-3(a) to condone the delay. As a matter of fact, the
controlling authority has referred to Exhibit P-3(a) (exhibit-Aa) in the order and it has to be legitimately presumed that
he applied his mind to this aspect. The appellate authority
also considered this aspect and observed that it must be
presumed that the controlling authority was satisfied with
the reasons stated for the delay. In the circumstances, I do
not think that there is any substance in this contention."
13. The said judgment is not of any help to
the petitioner, as the appeal filed by petitioner
has not been rejected on the ground that
separate delay condonation application was
not filed, but the ground of dismissal of the
appeal is that it was filed much beyond the
prescribed period.
14. In the present case, order was passed
by Controlling Authority on 18.12.2024 and
appeal against the order passed by Controlling
Authority was filed on 31.10.2025; the memo
of appeal filed by petitioner is absolutely silent
regarding 'cause of delay', and the factum of
composite appeal, filed by petitioner against
29 orders and return of such appeal by the
Appellate Authority vide letter dated
10.10.2025, is also not mentioned. Thus, the
reliance by petitioner on the aforesaid
judgment is clearly misplaced.
15. Provisions of Limitation Act do not apply
to proceedings under Payment of Gratuity Act,
therefore, there is no question of filing a delay
condonation application under Section 5 of the
Limitation Act in proceedings under Payment
of Gratuity Act. As per Statutory Scheme,
appeal against order passed under Section
7(4) of Payment of Gratuity Act has to be filed
within sixty days from the date of receipt of
order, however, the limitation period is

UKHC010167302026
2026:UHC:9108
extendable for a further period of sixty days.
An appeal filed after 120 days from the date
of receipt of the order, however, cannot be
entertained, as the Appellate Authority has
not been conferred the power to condone such
delay.
16. The order passed by Appellate Authority
is inconsonance with the provisions of
Payment of Gratuity Act, therefore, any
interference with Appellate Authority's order
would be unwarranted.
17. Accordingly, the writ petitions fail and
are dismissed.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J)
